summary: KERNEL CONTEST: The King James translation of the Bible (a fixed codified text) read by the KJV-Only movement as the exclusively inspired, inerrant transmission of divine will versus read by mainline/academic traditions as a historically situated, revisable translation. The contest determines who holds epistemic and institutional authority to adjudicate modern religious practice.

KERNEL CONTEST: A foundational constitutional framework (the codified kernel) read as establishing the judiciary as the ultimate, unchallengeable arbiter of legislative legitimacy (a judicial supremacy reading) versus a co-equal or parliament-subordinate reading. This contest defines the ultimate authority grounding of the state's coercive apparatus[cite: 2, 3].

KERNEL CONTEST: The Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (the shared international legal kernel) read as a strictly binding, reciprocal commitment requiring multilateral consensus to dissolve versus read as a provisional, transactional framework voidable upon unilateral perception of bad faith. Competing readings of the exact same treaty yield entirely different constraints regarding global sanctions and nuclear escalation[cite: 2].

human_readable: Jati System and Practice Norm Legitimation
summary: KERNEL CONTEST: The Jati occupational and social classification system (a deep practice-norm kernel) read by orthodox, centralized authorities as a rigid, textually mandated hierarchy versus read by localized communities through continuous drift, proliferation, and renegotiation. Tests the tension between an extractive formal authority structure and the reality of mutating community practice[cite: 2, 3].
